question.text: Ulaanbaatar is the capital of this Asian country, the center of a former empire led by Genghis Khan.
question.clue: The prince Kul Tigin is honored by 7th century inscriptions named for a river valley in this country's west, the Orkhon, which was a power center for the Gokturk state.

swap.text: Kazakhstan has the longest coastline on this body of water which, despite its name, is the largest lake in the world. This lake also borders Russia, Azerbaijan, Iran, and Turkmenistan, and caviar is often procured from fish in this lake.
swap.answerHtml: Caspian Sea [or Kaspii Tenizi, or Hazar Denzi, or Hezer Denizi]
swap.clue: The world's first oil tanker sailed across this body of water from a port that produced half of the world's oil in 1900.

question.leadin: The beginning of this war in 1979 led US president Jimmy Carter to boycott the 1980 Olympics in Moscow. --.
question.text: Identify this conflict between a communist power and a central Asian nation. The C.I.A. supplied the mujahedeen during this conflict.
question.clue: Operation Cyclone was an effort to fund one side in this conflict through the operation of the ISI, and was heavily promoted by men like Gust Avrakotos.

swap.leadin: Though it is not Iran, the Tehran Eight fought for this country in the 1980s.
swap.text: Name this country which the Soviet Union invaded in 1979.
swap.clue: One invasion of this country was ended by the Treaty of Gandamak and took place during the "Great Game."

question.leadin: Items such as an entire Quran inscribed within a ring were produced during this conqueror's namesake "Renaissance."
question.text: Name this Uzbek (OOZ-bek) warlord who, from his capital of Samarkand (SAA-mark-and), assembled an empire stretching from Delhi to Damascus in the late 14th century.
question.answerHtml: Tamerlane (TAM-er-lain) [or Tamerlame; or Timur the Lame; or Timūr Gurkānī; or Temür Küregen]
question.clue: In 1402, this general sparked the Ottoman Interregnum after defeating and capturing Bayezid the Thunderbolt.

swap.leadin: William Brydon was the sole survivor of a retreat made from this city to Jalalabad.
swap.text: Name this city ruled by leaders such as Shah Shujah Durrani. William Elphinstone's forces were massacred while retreating from this city in 1842.
swap.clue: A government in this city was established through the Peshawar Accord after the fall of Mohammad Najibullah.

question.leadin: This ruler forced the Assassins to surrender their fortress at Alamut, and killed hundreds of thousands in his sack of Baghdad.
question.text: Name this Mongol grandson of Genghis Khan who founded the Ilkhanate. The Mongol advance westward was stopped by his defeat at Ain Jalut by the Mamluks.
question.clue: This man's death occurred while fighting Berke, and he was succeeded by his son Abaqa.

swap.leadin: This general conquered the most land territory of any individual in history.
swap.text: Name this general, the longest-lived of Genghis Khan's "four dogs of war." He was key in Batu Khan's 1241 invasion of Europe.
swap.clue: This general was listed as one of the "four dogs of Temujin."

question.leadin: Answer the following about a certain country.
question.text: Primarily made up of three groups the Uzbeks, the Hazara, and the Tajiks, members of this military and political organization aided in overthrowing the Taliban and found key positions in Hamid Karzai's government.
question.answerHtml: The Northern Alliance [or The United Front for the Salvation of Afghanistan; or the UIF]

swap.leadin: This man from Transoxiana was the grandfather of the astronomer and mathematician Ulugh Beg.
swap.text: Name this ruler who started his imperial conquests with victories over the Chagatai Khanate. This leader defeated Tokhtamysh ("toke-tah-mish") at the Battle of the Terek River.
swap.clue: The only time an Ottoman Sultan was captured in battle was duringthis man's victory at the Battle of Ankara against Bayezid Thunderbolt.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the history of a mountainous nation that's been in the news a lot.
question.text: In 1893, the British set up this border between Afghanistan and Pakistan based on geographical features, not ethnic regions. This idiotic idea continues to lend itself today to ethnic tensions.
question.clue: The creation of this line, named for a British diplomat, effectively created a buffer zone between Britain and Russia in Asia. This line forms the de facto border between Afghanistan and Pakistan.

swap.text: Khublai Khan was the younger brother to this last Mongol to rule from Karakorum. His brother Hulagu led the western Mongol expansion past Iran to the Mediterranean, and he died while leading the conquest of China.
swap.clue: This ruler from the Toluid line subjected merchants to taxation and paid nobles in salaries as part of his administrative reform efforts.

question.leadin: Its historical importance extends to Darius' use of it to reach the Indus, and near it is the Shola stupa, a Buddhist temple known as its namesake "Top."
question.text: Identify this important pass through a major mountain range of Central Asia that was yielded to the British in the Treaty of Gandamak.
question.clue: Famously crossed by Alexander the Great, Darius I, and Genghis Khan, this pass links Pakistan and Afghanistan and was an integral part of the Silk Road.

swap.leadin: In his 2002 "Trashcanistan" article, Stephen Kotkin argues that this country is the only post-Soviet Central Asian state to not depend on Russia.
swap.text: Name this former Soviet Republic whose leader Rafiq Nishabov was removed by Moscow in 1989 after failing to stop ethnic violence against this country's Meskhetian Turks, which culminated in the Fergana massacre.
swap.answerHtml: Uzbekistan [or Republic of Uzbekistan; accept Oʻzbekiston Respublikasi; accept Uzbek Soviet Socialist Republic or Uzbek SSR or Uzbekskaja Sovetskaja Socialističeskaja Respublika or Oʻzbekiston Sovet Sotsialistik Respublikasi; accept Uzbekia]
swap.clue: In one event in this country, Chulpon Avenue was closed and hundred of people in Bobur Square were killed in a protest blamed on the Islamic group Akramia.

question.text: The Afghan side at Panipat was led by this ruler, who had previously invaded India as a general of Nader Shah. This ruler united the Pashtun tribes to form the first modern Afghan state under the Durrani dynasty.
question.answerHtml: Ahmad Shah Durrani [accept Ahmad Shah Abdali; prompt on Shah Durrani or Shah Abdali alone]
question.clue: This cavalry commander discovered the leader of the Afsharid kingdom assassinated in a tent, prompting him to abscond with the royal seal and the Koh-i-Noor diamond.

swap.text: Paizas were often carried by messengers traveling along this Mongolian postal system, which contained relay stations with supplies, shelter, and spare horses.

question.text: The Gokturks were led by this tribe and ruling dynasty. This tribe had been subjugated by the Rouran in 460, but conquered them in 552 under the leadership of Bumin Qaghan.

swap.text: Kublai's Semu ("suh-moo") caste included Buddhist Uyghurs from Qocho, who were Islamized by this state's khan Khizr Khoja. Turpan's Uyghurs built chunche raisin sheds after this Mongol khanate split into Moghulistan and Transoxiana.
swap.answerHtml: Chagatai Khanate [or Chagatai Ulus or Caġadai (“TSAH-gah-dye”) Ulus; or Chagatayids; accept Eastern Chagatai Khanate or Dōng Chágětái Hánguó]
swap.clue: This state's successor state of Moghulistan splintered into Yerkent and Turpan.

question.leadin: They conquered their namesake city after Alp Tigin was dismissed from office and used his slaves to take it over.
question.text: Identify this Islamic dynasty based out of Afghanistan that brought Islam to the heart of India under their greatest ruler Mahmud.
question.clue: One of the dynasties that sprung up in Transoxiana after the demise of the Abbasids was this one, whose founder Sabuktigin founded it by seizing Samanid territory. Its sultan Mahmud patronized the poet Ferdowsi.

swap.text: This Khereid princess became Genghis Khan's daughter-in-law when she married his youngest son Tolui. She was the mother of the khans Mongke, Kublai, and Hulagu.
